name: Adaptive Similarity Thresholding with Fallback Top-K Guarantee
description: RAG systems want high-confidence matches (similarity > 0.85) to avoid hallucinations, but if no document exceeds 0.85, they need a guaranteed top-1 fallback to provide at least some context.
prompt:
RAG systems want high-confidence matches (similarity > 0.85) to avoid hallucinations, but if no document exceeds 0.85, they need a guaranteed top-1 fallback to provide at least some context.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: kb_id, content, sim_score, rank_pos, match_type.
Results should be ordered as specified.
golden_sql:
-- Score items, guarantee top 1 fallback even if below 0.85 threshold
            WITH scored AS (
                SELECT 
                    kb_id,
                    content,
                    array_cosine_similarity(vector, [0.9, 0.2, 0.1]::FLOAT[3]) AS sim_score,
                    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY array_cosine_similarity(vector, [0.9, 0.2, 0.1]::FLOAT[3]) DESC) AS rank_pos
                FROM knowledge_base
            )
            SELECT 
                kb_id,
                content,
                ROUND(sim_score, 4) AS sim_score,
                rank_pos,
                CASE WHEN sim_score >= 0.85 THEN 'CONFIDENT_MATCH' ELSE 'FALLBACK_TOP_MATCH' END AS match_type
            FROM scored
            WHERE sim_score >= 0.85 OR rank_pos = 1
            ORDER BY rank_pos;
why_it_fails: A hard WHERE similarity > 0.85 yields empty sets, while a raw LIMIT 5 includes irrelevant noise.
